### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via index_status (literal, a string literal in KnowledgeRebuild), os knowledge rebuild (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts), os knowledge status (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/status.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via index_status (literal, a string literal in KnowledgeRebuild), os knowledge rebuild (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts), os knowledge status (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/status.ts))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0161cdcd1edd20886aead2878a3b38a87b12bed1` — the merge of head `3b351697d10880a91dd4a6bafce636e6c68b116f` into base `0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0161cdcd1edd20886aead2878a3b38a87b12bed1 && git checkout 0161cdcd1edd20886aead2878a3b38a87b12bed1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 3b351697d10880a91dd4a6bafce636e6c68b116f && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 && git merge --no-ff 3b351697d10880a91dd4a6bafce636e6c68b116f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `91e9a57551df14ae7ba4be6d17e6696fc2c90338`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37466 (body, triage, first touch, claim, os-dev report), the PR #37578 body and Acceptance notes, the net diff against `main` (5 files, +248/−51, CLI and docs only), and the 55 check-runs on the head: 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure. Required contexts are green (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and shards 1–10, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Design.** The PR takes the card's second option and makes no service change. That is right: `index_status` already returns `index` from the store and `build` (or `null`) from the answering node as separate fields (`knowledge-build-actions.ts:151-152`).
- **Public surface.** `os knowledge rebuild` gains `--timeout` (seconds, default 600, min 1). It now also makes one `index_status` read before `rebuild`, and only with `--wait`. Its exit codes change: a poll answered by another node no longer exits 1 on its own. `os knowledge status` changes one output line. Nothing is removed or renamed, and no option is refused that was accepted before.
- **No false success: mostly holds.** Success comes from the build's own `done` record, or from the index turning `current` after a baseline that was not `current`. A missing baseline state counts as `current` (`rebuild.ts:109`), so it never yields success. A same-fingerprint rebuild waits for the building node's record, which is correct because neither adapter opens a `building` generation for it. `failed` and `not-run` records still exit 1 (`rebuild.ts:135`). Two paths still give a false exit 0:
  - **S2 (should-fix): baseline judged by `state` instead of `due`.** `indexWasCurrent` is `state === 'current'`, so any other state counts as a valid "was not current" baseline. `unreadable` is one of those states, and `readIndexState` returns it when the adapter read throws (`knowledge-service.ts:890`), so it can be transient. Take a transient error on the baseline read of a same-fingerprint rebuild: the next poll on another node reads `current` and exits 0 saying "a complete build has recorded itself", while this build is still running and may still fail. Separately, `unknown`, `listed-*`, `not-built-here` and a `no-recipe-hash` with no `completeBuild` never turn `current`, so for those the line "(waiting for it to turn current)" can only end on `--timeout`. Fix: take the fallback exit only when `indexBefore?.due === true`, which is exactly the never-built, new-fingerprint, recipe-changed and no-recipe-hash-with-completeBuild set the docblock names. Treat every other state like `current`. Add a test with an `unreadable` baseline followed by a `current` poll on another node, and assert no exit 0.
  - **S3 (should-fix): the premise does not hold for the `memory` adapter.** The code, docs and status line all say the store's index state is "the same on every node". That is true for `pgvector`. It is false for the default `memory` adapter, whose index is a per-process `Map` (`knowledge-memory/src/index.ts:91`). Behind a load balancer the baseline can come from a node whose memory index is due (restarted, boot build not yet done, or `buildAtBoot: false`). A later poll can then land on a node whose own memory index is `current`, and the command exits 0 while the build on the third node runs. Fix: do not take the index-current exit when the source's `adapter` is `memory` (the view carries it). In `cli.mdx` (the status and rebuild paragraphs) and the status line, say the index is the same on every node only when the adapter's store is shared.
- **Poll loop.** There is no tight spin: every pass waits `--interval` seconds (min 1) before its read. The no-record wait is bounded by `--timeout` and resets only on a read of this build's record, so a single-node build is never cut off. A build that stays `running` on its node is followed for as long as it runs, as before. Every read failure still exits 1 at once, as before.
  - **N1 (nit):** `--timeout` counts reads times `--interval`, not wall-clock time, and `runKnowledgeAction` (not in the diff) sets no request timeout. A request that hangs is therefore not bounded by `--timeout`. The flag text and the docs describe this accurately, so it is a note, not a defect.
- **Stale or older records.** A record with another `startedAt` is read as no record (tested). `startedAt` is always present on a real server, because `rebuildSource` sets the record synchronously (`knowledge-service.ts:924-931`). The `startedAt === undefined` branch only covers an older server.
- **Tests: real controls.** The 6 new cases cover each branch with a negative control. A `current` baseline never exits 0 from the index; the build's own recorded failure still exits 1; `--timeout 4` against `--interval 2` exits on exactly the 2nd unseen read; and the reset case turns red if the reset is removed. The ablation result (9 of 12 red when `rebuild.ts` is put back to the base) explains as follows:
  - The 3 that stay green: the two `os knowledge status` cases, because the ablation restored only `rebuild.ts` and `status.ts` kept the PR's text. Also the `--no-wait` case: the new baseline read is gated on `flags.wait` (`rebuild.ts:86`), so its single-request sequence is the same on base.
  - Of the 9 red, 3 are older rebuild cases ("follows it to its end", "did not finish", "refusal text"). They turn red only because the fixture gained a baseline response that base hands to `rebuild`. That is a fixture shift, not behaviour, so the behavioural evidence is the 6 new cases. That is enough.
  - The status text change has no ablation reading, but its assertion pins the new line ("none recorded there"), which the base line would fail.
  - None of the 12 covers an `unreadable` baseline (S2).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/cli` is right: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right too, because nothing a metadata author writes changes.
- **S1 (should-fix): the `Clause-②:` line is wrong.** `@objectstack/cli` is a published package: `publishConfig.access: public`, not private, bin `os`, ships `dist`. Its command options are public surface, and scripts call them. The seat's precedent agrees: on #37099 (PR #37439) new CLI commands were `Clause-②: yes`, and on #37485 a new public URL parameter was `Clause-②: yes`. A new `--timeout` flag is the same kind of change.
  - The line should be `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in both the PR body and the changeset body. The level stays `patch`, and no BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
  - This is not cosmetic. `release-github-releases.mjs` files a `Clause-②: yes` widening under 新增能力 and a `no` under 其他修复, so the release notes would hide the new flag.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- **Accepted limit 1: no node identity in `index_status`.** Acceptable, and no card needed. It limits labelling only: `status` now says "the node that answered", which is true, and it says when that node holds no record. Adding a node id to the answer is a service change outside this card. A shared build record (the card's first option) would remove the limit.
- **Accepted limit 2: a failed build seen only through other nodes ends on `--timeout`.** Acceptable, and no card needed. Exit 1 is the right code for a failure; it only comes late, and the message honestly says the build may still be running. The same timeout also catches a successful same-fingerprint rebuild whose reads never reach the building node. At the default that needs about 300 reads in a row to miss one node, which is negligible under round-robin. File the shared build record only if an operator reports the wait.
- Dev flags: the two `out_of_scope_findings` are these two limits, answered above. `dogfood_battery` n/a is right: no `!` and no narrowing arm. `security_findings`: none, agreed; the admin gate is unchanged and server-side.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff is CLI and docs only, with no data access, id materialisation or join.
- Owed before merge: S1 (two declaration lines), S2 (a one-line predicate and one test), S3 (an adapter check or a docs qualification). N1 is optional.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3b351697d10880a91dd4a6bafce636e6c68b116f`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review on `91e9a575` (record 7194806473; seat REWORK 7194818791). I read the delta diff `91e9a575..3b351697`, the net diff against `main` (still 5 files, now +306/−51, CLI and docs only), the PR body as edited at 15:09:57Z, the changeset, dev report 7195831596, and the check-runs on the new head.

The check-runs on the new head are 40 success, 17 skipped, 0 failure, and 2 re-runs started by the body edit:
- PR-body guards: the re-run is `success`.
- Check Changeset: the re-run is still `in_progress`. Its first run on this same head (14:38Z) was `success`, but that run read the body while it still said `Clause-②: no`. The seat should see the re-run green before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S2 — closed.** The fallback now exits only when the baseline said `due === true` and the adapter is not `memory` (`indexCanTell`). An `unreadable`, `current`, unread or never-current baseline now waits for the building node's record, so the false exit 0 is gone. The new test is a real control: an `unreadable` baseline, then two `current` polls elsewhere, ends on `--timeout` with no "The index is current". The dev's ablation, putting the state-based predicate back, turns only this case red.
- **S3 — closed.** With adapter id `memory`, the index state is never taken as the build's end, and the line says why. The docs (status and rebuild paragraphs), the status line and the docblocks now say the index is the same on every node only for a shared store (`pgvector`).
  - The new test is a real control: a `memory` baseline that is due, then a `current` poll with no record, is not an exit 0, and the building node's `done` decides. The dev's ablation, forcing the check false, turns only this case red.
  - The status test pins the new line ("not on the memory adapter").
- **N1 — stays open, accepted.** Nothing changed. The PR's Acceptance notes now name it.
- **N2 (nit, new): one wrong comment.** The comment at `rebuild.ts` `indexCanTell` says every `due: true` state turns `current` at a build's end. `listed-empty` is `due: true` (an adapter with `listDocuments` and no `indexStatus`), and it becomes `listed-documents`, never `current`.
  - The only effect: on such an adapter the line "(waiting for it to turn current)" can end only on the building node's record or on `--timeout`. There is no false exit 0, because `current` comes only from `indexStatus`.
  - Fix if touched again: name `listed-empty` among the states that leave the record as the only answer.
- **Nothing else moved.** The poll loop, timeout reset and record matching are unchanged from the head already reviewed. No tight spin and no unbounded no-record wait.

### ② Semver level

- **S1 — closed.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` now stands at line start in both the changeset body and the PR body, and the two agree. The level stays `patch` on `@objectstack/cli`, which is right: a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` stands. The changeset text now also states the shared-store and not-`memory` conditions, which matches the code. No BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- **Memory check by id only** (the dev's out-of-scope finding, now in the PR's Acceptance notes): acceptable, and not worth a card on its own.
  - `knowledge-memory`'s plugin does accept `opts.id` (`knowledge-memory/src/index.ts:422`), so a renamed memory adapter is possible. But a false exit 0 then needs a multi-node deployment on a renamed per-process adapter, a due baseline and a poll that lands on another node whose own index is `current`. That deployment re-embeds the source on every node anyway.
  - The real fix is server-side: the adapter or `index_status` says whether its index is shared. That belongs with the card's first option (a shared build record) if that is ever filed. The Acceptance note is the right carrier for now.
- The two original accepted limits stand as judged in record 7194806473.
- SQL push-down: not applicable (CLI and docs only).
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: nothing in the delta touches auth or the admin gate, and the delta has nothing to withhold. The seat may ask the dev to restate it as `none`.
